channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: South Korea's power utility KEPCO confirms a breach that exposed data on 1.52 million people, including bank and card numbers
item.description: Korea Electric Power Corporation says an intruder took personal data on about 1.52 million customers, suppliers and staff from its billing platform and procurement system; the privacy regulator has opened an investigation. (Seoul Economic Daily, Seoul Economic Daily (regulator probe), BleepingComputer)

item.title: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive less than two weeks after his resignation
item.description: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO and president, saying input from senior US government officials convinced it that his return poses no national security risk. (TechCrunch, The Register)

item.title: Amazon buys Decart's chip-optimization software and hires its founders as it prepares to sell Trainium chips to customers
item.description: Amazon is acquiring the Decart Optimization Stack, software that tunes AI workloads for specific chips, along with Decart's founders and engineers, in a deal Bloomberg values at about $7.5 billion. (TechCrunch, The Register)

item.title: German media report that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed anti-satellite weapon into orbit as early as December
item.description: NDR, WDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung report that Western intelligence agencies believe Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, which would threaten thousands of spacecraft in low Earth orbit; the Kremlin dismisses the claim. (Ars Technica, AeroTime)

item.title: Interrupt-Aware Static Detection of Deadlocks in Rust Operating Systems
item.description: A static analysis that tracks both held locks and interrupt state in Rust kernels, paired with an AI agent that audits its reports, found nine maintainer-confirmed deadlock bugs in four Rust operating systems. (Yuzhi Li, Hongliang Tian, Chengjun Chen et al. · Fudan University; Ant Group)

item.title: FDA rejects Capricor's Duchenne cell therapy a second time, citing unreliable data from its phase 3 trial
item.description: The FDA declined again to approve deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, saying the phase 3 HOPE-3 trial missed its prespecified goals and that inspection findings made its data unreliable. (Pharmacally, NeurologyLive, Capricor (July 2025 release, background))

item.title: Virginia reports its first measles death of 2026, a young child, as confirmed US cases reach 5,838
item.description: Virginia health officials reported the death of a child aged four or younger who had measles, the 12th such death reported by US states this year, as the CDC's national count reached 5,838 cases. (Virginia Department of Health, CDC, ABC News, The Guardian)

item.title: Merck's antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT extends survival in heavily pretreated stomach and oesophageal cancer, the company says
item.description: Merck says its 473-patient phase 3 TroFuse-015 trial of sacituzumab tirumotecan met its overall survival goal in third-line gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, but missed on progression-free survival and released no numbers. (BioPharm International, OncoDaily, The Pharma Letter, Merck)

item.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis
item.description: A platform trial in 401 adults with tuberculosis screened ten new four-drug combinations at once and selected two 16-week regimens, each built around a new drug, for further testing. (Hanif Esmail Nicholas I. Paton Jodie A. Schildkraut Ilaria Motta Alexander J. Szubert Suzanne M. Dufault Norbert Heinrich Simon Tiberi Cissy M. Kityo Timothy D. McHugh Fairoez Ryklief Daniela M. Cirillo Rodney Dawson Karen Sanders Stellah Mpagama Lindsay C. Thompson Le Hong Van Dominic Wakerley Elena Tudor Angela M. Crook Patrick P.J. Phillips Guy Thwaites Christoph Lange Martin J. Boeree Gareth Maher-Edwards Natasa Lazarevic Jolanda E. van de Logt Derek J. Sloan David Barros-Aguirre and Michael Hoelscherthe PARADIGM4TB (UNITE4TB-01) Trial Team* · University College London; Radboud University Medical Center; National University of Singapore; LMU University Hospital Munich; GSK)

item.title: Multiscale spatial atlas of human basal ganglia cell types and communities
item.description: A spatial map of about 7.9 million cells in four human brains resolves 60 cell types in the basal ganglia and shows how they are arranged, part of a 26-study atlas of the region. (Bereket Tesfay Berackey, Zhiqun Tan, Ginny Wu et al. · University of California, Irvine)

item.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
item.description: Three cryo-electron microscopy structures show that the hormone relaxin-2 and a small-molecule drug candidate, AZD5462, switch on the same receptor by binding different parts of it and reshaping it differently. (James Osei-Owusu, Tristan Girbau, Xunan Wang et al. · Harvard Medical School)

item.title: COP31 ends without an overall agreement after the EU and island states reject a text that does not name fossil fuels
item.description: The UN climate summit in Antalya closed on Sunday with its main political text unadopted, the first such outcome since 2000, after a dispute over whether to mention fossil fuels. (Phys.org (AFP), Health Policy Watch)

item.title: Robot dives beside the Challenger Deep recover the deepest explosive volcanic deposits ever documented
item.description: Seven remotely operated dives on the Mariana Trench wall found rocks from explosive eruptions at more than 6,000 metres depth, in a zone where young volcanism is not expected. (Frontiers in Earth Science, Phys.org)

item.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
item.description: Measurements from 21 research cruises and a global chemistry model put atmospheric organic nitrogen falling on the oceans at 12.8 million tonnes a year, about 27% of all nitrogen deposition. (Xu Yu, Yumin Li, Guitao Shi et al. · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; East China Normal University; Ocean University of China; South China University of Technology)

item.title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
item.description: Chips smaller than a grain of rice sit inside test tubes and wirelessly report the temperature of a chemical reaction every half-second. (Sukwoo Lee, Evan A. Weingarten, Michael F. Reynolds et al. · Stanford University; Cornell University; Emory University; OWiC Technologies)

item.title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
item.description: Radio observations of gas swirling at the centre of the most luminous known obscured quasar give the first motion-based mass for a supermassive black hole beyond redshift 2. (Mai Liao, Roberto J. Assef, Chao-Wei Tsai et al.)

item.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9 billion
item.description: CrowdStrike will pay 1.135 of its shares for each Zscaler share, a 34% premium, to add network security to its device-security platform; its own shares fell more than 8% premarket. (Zscaler (joint press release), The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Taiwan eases margin-call rules as Asian authorities try to halt an AI-driven stock rout
item.description: After the Taiex lost 17.5% in a week, Taiwan cut the margin-maintenance threshold to 120% from 130%, tightened short-selling rules and kept its stabilization fund in the market; the index rebounded 2.16% on Monday. (Focus Taiwan (CNA), Focus Taiwan (CNA), The Globe and Mail (Reuters))

item.title: Trump threatens a "tremendous tax" on US companies that build AI data centres abroad
item.description: President Trump said US firms that build data centres overseas would face a heavy tax, but gave no details and said his staff were hearing the idea for the first time. (BBC, The Globe and Mail (AP))

item.title: A Missouri judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement of Roundup cancer claims
item.description: A St Louis state court found the deal "fair, reasonable and adequate", potentially ending most of the litigation that has weighed on Bayer since it bought Monsanto in 2018. (The Guardian, Insurance Journal)

item.title: Past Automation and Future AI: How Weak Links Tame the Growth Explosion
item.description: Jones and Tonetti find that automation explains essentially all US productivity growth since 1950, and that AI should speed growth up, but slowly, because tasks still done by people hold the economy back. (Charles I. Jones, Christopher Tonetti · Stanford GSB, Anthropic, NBER)

item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared metric for industry limits on AI development, and publishes OpenAI's own numbers
item.description: Jakub Pachocki argues that held-out perplexity should become a cross-lab measure of progress, discloses OpenAI's internal figures, and proposes limits that labs would not cross until monitoring improves. (OpenAI, TechCrunch)

item.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
item.description: Inserting search queries and retrieved passages into ordinary pretraining text teaches small language models to search and to trust evidence, an advantage that later fine-tuning on search data does not fully reproduce. (Kaustubh Ponkshe, Gyung Hyun Je, Stefan Taga et al. · EPFL, University of Toronto)

item.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
item.description: Each RL-trained expert model is distilled into 256 learned input vectors on a frozen base model, and experts combine simply by concatenating those prompts, matching full multi-teacher distillation. (Zhen Zhang, Changyi Yang, Xuehai He et al. · University of California, Santa Barbara, Carnegie Mellon University)

item.title: Neural Geometry as a Learning Signal
item.description: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B only to make an internal representation match its idealized circle or helix, with no loss on outputs, improves task accuracy about as much as ordinary fine-tuning. (Eric Todd, Tal Haklay, Nikhil Prakash et al. · Northeastern University, University of Southern California, University of Amsterdam)

item.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
item.description: BioEmu2 is one diffusion model that predicts biomolecular structures, samples their equilibrium ensembles and jumps forward in time, covering proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and ions far faster than molecular dynamics. (Michael Gastegger, Adam E. Foster, José Jiménez-Luna et al. · Microsoft)

item.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models
item.description: Planning longer with a latent world model can turn working plans into adversarial examples of the model; checking that planned actions can be read back from predicted states largely fixes it. (Huiyuan Tian, Chih-Yung Wen, Shijian Li · Zhejiang University, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

item.title: The FBI investigates an apparent breach of NCIC, the database police across the US use to check warrants and stolen property
item.description: CNN and the Associated Press report that the FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center; the bureau has not confirmed it and the scope is unknown. (BleepingComputer, TechCrunch)

item.title: Microsoft says attackers exploited an Entra Connect Health flaw to read administrator email addresses and tenant details
item.description: A flaw in Microsoft's Entra Connect Health API, present from July 23 until a fix on November 19, let outsiders read administrator contacts and tenant metadata; passwords and tokens were not exposed. (BleepingComputer, Daily CyberSecurity)

item.title: The FCC overrides California's landline rules, clearing AT&T to drop copper phone service for about 184,000 homes
item.description: The FCC ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort rules against AT&T, which wants to end basic copper phone service for 184,000 residential and 15,000 business customers in June 2027. (Ars Technica, Broadband Breakfast)

item.title: A blood protein flags advanced CTE in former football players, a small JAMA study finds
item.description: In 21 former football players who later donated their brains, blood levels of a tau protein fragment were far higher in those with advanced CTE, a preliminary step toward diagnosing the disease in life. (The Boston Globe, AZFamily)

item.title: FDA approves Regeneron's Livsayis, the first gene-silencing drug for generalized myasthenia gravis
item.description: The FDA approved cemdisiran (Livsayis), an injection given four times a year that silences production of the immune protein C5, for adults with antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. (Medical Daily, WebMD, BioPharm International)

item.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
item.description: Recordings from 28 surgical patients show a small spot in Wernicke's area, long seen as a listening region, activates about a quarter-second before each spoken word and is needed for speaking. (Alexander B. Silva, Matthew K. Leonard, Patrick W. Hullett et al. · University of California, San Francisco)

item.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
item.description: Teeth from two caves in Guangxi, dated to between about 324,000 and 184,000 years ago, show Homo erectus survived in southern China's rainforests much later than its previously known disappearance from mainland Asia. (Wei Liao, Clément Zanolli, Ragnheiður Diljá Ásmundsdóttir et al.)

item.title: EPFL theory predicts the heating power fusion plasmas need to enter high-confinement mode
item.description: Physicists at EPFL's Swiss Plasma Center have a single theory for the power needed to push tokamak plasmas into high-confinement mode, and say ITER has margin while SPARC is close to its limit. (Phys.org (EPFL release), arXiv (De Lucca et al.))

item.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
item.description: In a defect-free superfluid of ultracold atoms, widening a narrow channel first lowers its resistance and then, as the channel turns from one- to two-dimensional, raises it again, with a resistance minimum in between. (Simon Wili, Meng-Zi Huang, Tommaso Bonaccorsi et al.)

item.title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
item.description: A flat cloud of ultracold potassium atoms simulates a massive relativistic quantum field in two dimensions of space, showing a tunable mass gap and topological domain walls, a step toward lab tests of early-universe physics. (Yansheng Zhang, Feiyang Wang, Paul H. C. Wong et al.)

item.title: An AI sell-off pushes the S&P 500 and the Dow into a correction as Nvidia falls about 14%
item.description: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.28% on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow into a correction and erasing the Nasdaq's gains for the year as AI stocks slumped. (Fox Business, Yahoo Finance, Quartz)

item.title: The UK and EU agree deals on food trade, carbon markets and youth mobility, but tuition fees remain unresolved
item.description: The UK and EU agreed to ease Brexit checks on food, relink their emissions trading schemes and create a youth mobility scheme, in exchange for UK alignment with EU rules in those areas. (The Guardian, BBC)

item.title: Intuit agrees to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, less than a third of what it paid
item.description: Intuit will sell email marketing platform Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, less than a third of the roughly $12 billion it paid in 2021, and use the cash to buy back shares. (Intuit, TechCrunch)

item.title: Canadian retail sales rise 0.8% in September on higher gas prices, but an early estimate points to a 1.5% drop in October
item.description: Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% to $75.3 billion in September, mostly on higher prices at gas stations, while sales volumes rose just 0.1% and an early estimate shows a 1.5% fall in October. (Statistics Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Gambling for Goals
item.description: Using a survey linked to millions of Korean credit, telecom and card records, economists find that people who see life goals like homeownership as out of reach take more financial risks, such as trading crypto. (Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel et al.)

item.title: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims a Lean-formalized proof of the Riemann hypothesis, found working with Claude
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis and formalized it in Lean; outside mathematicians report the code compiles, but no human-readable proof exists yet. (Levent Alpöge, The Verge, TechCrunch)

item.title: Google rolls out Genie 4, its most realistic interactive world model, to Google AI Ultra subscribers
item.description: Google DeepMind's Genie 4 world model reaches paying users in Project Genie, letting them edit generated worlds mid-session with text prompts and adding real-time native audio. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
item.description: PMD distills diffusion models into four-step generators that keep the teacher's diversity, by matching "tilted" posterior means that each cost a single teacher call at a shifted input. (Hidir Yesiltepe, Julius Berner, Arash Vahdat et al. · Virginia Tech, NVIDIA)

item.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
item.description: Stream of Belief lets several copies of a frozen LLM reason together by exchanging probability-weighted "belief tokens" instead of text, iterating until their joint state stops changing. (Yu Yao, Jiayi Dong, Yilun Du · MIT, UCLA, Harvard)

item.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
item.description: Gamer is a vision-language-action model that plays complex 3D games in real time from raw screen pixels with keyboard and mouse, trained by continued pre-training, sparse-reasoning fine-tuning and long-horizon RL. (Run Luo, Kuan Zhang, Qi Deng et al. · miHoYo, National University of Singapore, Tsinghua University)

item.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
item.description: By deliberately breaking simulated users and checking whether metrics notice, this paper shows existing user-simulator evaluations miss many failures, and proposes a suite that catches all ten tested. (Hengguang Zhou, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen et al.)

item.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
item.description: DNeo, a parallel draft model for speculative decoding, fixes how drafters read the target model's hidden states and remembers rejected drafts, generating up to 1.3 times faster than the previous best. (Jameson Sandler, Shane Bergsma, Mostafa Elhoushi et al.)

item.title: F5 issues emergency hotfixes for critical BIG-IP flaws that can crash traffic handling and may allow remote code execution
item.description: F5 released out-of-band hotfixes for critical, unauthenticated BIG-IP flaws that can crash its traffic engine and may allow remote code execution; no mitigations exist besides patching. (BleepingComputer, Canadian Centre for Cyber Security)

item.title: Amazon says suspected Chinese hackers used the AI agent framework Cairn to find and exploit a zero-day at East Asian universities
item.description: Amazon found an exposed Cairn server showing AI agents that worked for hours without human direction, then discovered and used an unknown flaw in a medical imaging app to take over university servers. (The Record, The Register)

item.title: UK surveillance tribunal confirms the Home Office served Apple a secret order over encrypted iCloud data
item.description: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's secrecy argument and confirmed it served Apple a Technical Capability Notice, though the order's content stays secret ahead of a 2027 hearing. (Investigatory Powers Tribunal judgment, The Register)

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots by default to keep Siri and Gemini agents from reading private chats
item.description: Signal's iOS and Android apps now block screenshots by default so built-in AI agents cannot capture chats, and the company says operating systems give developers no robust way to stop such access. (The Register, Engadget)

item.title: Polymorph: Operating System Kernel Optimization Through Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Polymorph has an AI agent write one tunable Linux kernel policy, then tunes it live without a language model, beating Linux's defaults for page caching and scheduling at far lower cost than offline search. (Dean Sysman, Georgios Liargkovas, Tal Zussman et al.)

item.title: A daily KRAS-blocking pill plus chemotherapy stops tumour growth in 90% of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer in an early trial
item.description: In a 61-patient phase 1/2 trial, daraxonrasib plus standard chemotherapy shrank tumours in just over 60% of people newly diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; 76.6% were alive at one year. (BBC News, The Guardian)

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Nelkarmi for ALK-positive lung cancer that has outgrown earlier drugs
item.description: The FDA cleared neladalkib, a daily pill, for advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer after earlier ALK inhibitors stop working, based on response rates of 49% and 32% in a 222-patient trial. (pharmaphorum, chemXplore)

item.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
item.description: In two phase 3 trials with 1,019 adults with obesity and painful knee osteoarthritis, weekly retatrutide injections cut pain scores and body weight significantly more than placebo, with more serious side effects. (Thomas J. Schnitzer David J. Hunter Philip G. Conaghan Arya M. Sharma Sue D. Pedersen Kaiyi Chen So Young Park Nune Makarova Kathryn Giblin and Tammy Forresterthe TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA Investigators* · Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine; University of Sydney; University of Leeds; University of Alberta; University of Calgary; Eli Lilly and Company)

item.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
item.description: A DNA recorder inserted into a fertilized mouse egg wrote an ordered log of cell divisions into the genome, letting researchers rebuild a mouse embryo's cell family tree from the first division to organ formation. (Qi Yu, Haedong Kim, Sophie Seidel et al. · University of Washington School of Medicine; Howard Hughes Medical Institute; Dartmouth College)

item.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
item.description: Mapping where each cell type sits in the basal ganglia of humans, macaques and marmosets, researchers found a highly stereotyped layout shared across primates and often with mice, with gene gradients laid over discrete compartments. (Madeleine N. Hewitt, Meghan A. Turner, Nelson Johansen et al. · Allen Institute for Brain Science; Princeton Neuroscience Institute; Leiden University Medical Center; Delft University of Technology; The Rockefeller University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Washington University in St. Louis; RIKEN; Kyoto University; University of Washington)

item.title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury after an eight-year voyage and prepares to become the second spacecraft ever to orbit it
item.description: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission has arrived at Mercury after more than eight years and is set to fire its thrusters to enter orbit, with science operations due to begin in April. (The Guardian, BBC News)
